paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. The first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027.

**On 21/11/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, in the 19:58 UTC reading, Polymarket pays 46.75 and Kalshi 50.00. In the 86 first-round lists with fieldwork ending between 07/10 and 17/11, from 8 pollsters, she is first in all of them, with 27% to 40%, and she leads in the 39 runoff matchups in which she was tested in that period, with 52% to 70%. The two most recent polls in the database are still YouGov's for Le HuffPost, with fieldwork from 12 to 17/11, and Ifop-Fiducial's for TF1-LCI, Le Figaro and Sud Radio, with fieldwork from 13 to 16/11. Notice 10392, from Ifop-Fiducial for Sud Radio, with fieldwork from 2 to 4/11, published by the Commission des sondages on 20/11, has still not been structured by the database and is not in this screen's counts. Le Pen's appeal against ineligibility at the Cour de cassation is due to be decided by early April 2027.

**Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average and 3rd in the Polymarket win contract.** In the polls, he averages 18.1 across 42 lists from 7 pollsters with fieldwork ending between 22/10 and 17/11, and is among the top two in 80 of the 86 lists from 07/10 to 17/11; in the 14 runoff matchups in which he was tested in that period, he trails in all of them, with 30% to 39%. In the win contract, he is at 14.50 on Polymarket and 12.00 on Kalshi.

**Two names in the top five of both markets appear in fewer than half of the 86 lists: David Lisnard in 40, and Christine Lagarde in 2.** Lisnard is 2nd on Polymarket, at 17.15, and at 16.00 on Kalshi; in the polls, he is not among the top two in any of the 40 lists and averages 9.2 across 29 lists from 7 pollsters with fieldwork ending between 22/10 and 17/11. Lagarde is 5th on Polymarket, at 3.85, and at 6.00 on Kalshi; the two lists that test her are from Cluster17 for Politico, with fieldwork on 9 and 10/11, and give her 14% and 8%. Lagarde is not a declared candidate; on 29/10, the European Central Bank announced that she leaves the bank's presidency on 07/02/2027. Teddy Riner, who announced his candidacy on 09/11, is at 0.75 on Polymarket and 2.00 on Kalshi; he appears in 5 of the 86 lists, one from each of 5 pollsters, with 2% to 4.5%; in the two most recent, he has 3% in YouGov's and 4% in Ifop's.

**Édouard Philippe and Raphaël Glucksmann are less than one point apart in the poll average; in the Polymarket win contract, Philippe's price is more than three times Glucksmann's.** Philippe averages 12.3 across 30 lists from 7 pollsters with fieldwork ending between 22/10 and 17/11, and Glucksmann 11.6, across 41 lists from 7 pollsters; in the 86 lists from 07/10 to 17/11, Philippe appears in 60 and is among the top two in 3, and Glucksmann appears in 81 and is among the top two in 3. In the win contract, Philippe is at 4.50 on Polymarket and 4.70 on Kalshi, and Glucksmann at 1.45 and 1.00.

**In the 18:25 UTC press collection of 21/11, seven of the ten headlines, from 10 outlets, are about François Ruffin's withdrawal of his candidacy.** In a statement posted on X on 21/11, the MP wrote "Face au risque du pire, je retire ma candidature à l'élection présidentielle" (faced with the risk of the worst, I withdraw my candidacy for the presidential election); he says that "les appareils ont rejeté cette grande primaire" (the party machines rejected this great primary) of the whole left, which he had called for, and wishes "bon courage et bonne campagne" (good luck and a good campaign) to the left-wing candidates still in the race, without endorsing any of them. Le Monde, Le Figaro, Libération, France 24, L'Express, L'Opinion and Le HuffPost report it. Ruffin appears in 8 of the 86 first-round lists with fieldwork ending between 07/10 and 17/11, from 4 pollsters, with 1.5% to 3%; the most recent is Ifop-Fiducial's, with fieldwork from 13 to 16/11. In the Polymarket contract on who will be on the ballot, he was at 13.50 in the reading of 20/11 at 20:47 UTC and is at 3.30 in the 19:58 UTC reading of 21/11. The other three headlines are about the primary of the right and centre: franceinfo and BFMTV report that the campaign directors of Gabriel Attal, Bruno Retailleau and David Lisnard meet again on Thursday 26/11, and Le JDD's headline says Édouard Philippe "fait cavalier seul" (is going it alone). According to franceinfo, citing Attal's entourage, two date options for the two rounds have consensus, 17 and 24/01 or 24 and 31/01, with mostly electronic voting and 2 euros per voter; Philippe still rejects the primary, and his team remains invited to the meetings.

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, it does not turn a price into a voting intention, and it does not show a poll number without its checked official notice. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as French law of 1977 requires.
